description:
S01 E07 — 3D Printing Technology and Cloud Storage
Deep diving into 3D Printing technology and cloud storage; discovering about Trains, Mammals, an aerosol spray and signs and treatments of the Common Cold.

description:
S01 E08 — What Makes a Storm?
A look at the many woodwind instruments; exploring the benefits of tablet computers; finding out what makes a storm; covering the history of speakers and rubbing alcohol; finding out about the planets.

title: More Curious?
description:
S01 E09 — What Are the Many Functions of Our Nose?
Bass describes musical instruments with a low or deep frequency, passports are essential for global travel and the many functions of our nose; other topics covered include blood pressure, cinema, pop and comics.

description:
Winds of Change
Traveling to India and Denmark to explore two innovative movements that are helping to drive down greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Earthrise
description:
Human-Wildlife Conflict
Earthrise travels to Bangladesh and Australia, to visit two projects that have found ways for humans and animals to live better together on our shared planet.

title: Earthrise
description:
Life After Conflict
We explore the environmental consequences of war and how different people from Rohingya refugees to Syrian scientists are trying to restore a healthy relationship with nature.

Kay Nambiar and the team investigate paranormal activity in London's 'Ragged School' and abandoned Woolwich Arsenal.

The transformation is complete, and it's time for the Flying Kestrel to be put to the test.

The owner of Kestrel Beer buys an original 1930s Riley Kestrel, with the intention of restoring it and then breaking the land-speed record.

With the advent and spread of airplanes and automobiles in the beginning of the 20th century an idea emerged that a marriage of the two would create the ultimate travel miracle.

A defiant all-girls space-tech school aims to build Kyrgyzstan's first satellite, a country where girls are often kidnapped and forced to marry.

description:
Ecuador's Hidden Treasure
Three female scientists investigate Ecuador's endangered spider monkeys and empower indigenous women in a scientific area usually dominated by men.

title: Women Make Science
description:
From The Lab To The Field
Dr Sheila Ochugboju takes her scientific knowledge to Kenya to turn parasitic problems into scientific solutions.

title: Future Warfare
description:
S01 E04
Modern warfare has leaped forth into the era of supercomputers, satellite surveillance and artificial intelligence; Special Operations soldiers have come out of the trenches and are entering new domains of warfare.

description:
S04 E01 — Mercury or Bust
The JAXA-ESA joint BepiColombo Mission aims to shed new light on the strange and tiny world of Mercury.

title: The New Frontier
description:
S04 E05 — Hyabusa
The Japanese Asteroid Sample Return Mission reaches its target to collect rock samples to aid scientists in the development in planetary defense systems.

title: The New Frontier
description:
S04 E06 — Eyes to the Heavens
Two new space telescopes, Gaia and TESS, are in orbit with their primary missions coming to a close, then they will be joined by the James Webb Telescope, and together it is hoped they will open up a whole new vista into time and space.

S01 E02 — Secrets Of McVities Biscuits
McVitie's factory in Carlisle, Cumbria, opens its doors to reveal how millions of the nation's favourite biscuits are made, 24 hours a day, in one of Britain's biggest factories and one of the oldest biscuit factories in the world.

title: Secrets of the Factories
description:

An insight into Heinz's Wigan plant, a factory that produces 1.3 million cans of beans a day, and 128,000 tonnes of soup.

description:

The Mr. Kipling factory in Carlton, near Barnsley in Yorkshire, opens its doors to reveal how millions of the nation's favorite cakes are made in one of Britain's biggest factories - which is also the biggest cake factory Europe.
